display.purpose: The recipe name, once per page, in the headnote.

headline.purpose: The version line under the name; the batch row’s churned date; a later batch’s date.

body.purpose: Headnote prose, method instructions, authored notes. Lead-ins bold within the same size.

section.purpose: Region names and block legends — a true heading weight, not a label.

label.purpose: Table headers and the running head. The plain, unweighted sibling of Caption.

caption.purpose: Every caption that labels an input: field captions, batch cell labels, axis names, segmented captions, the two group cues. Uppercase by text-transform so the source stays sentence case.

control.purpose: Actionable choices, text controls, segmented options, hint and status sentences.

helper.purpose: A helper sentence beside a caption, never inside it — sentence case, always a sibling of the uppercase caption element.

table.purpose: Ingredient table cells, the graduated rule label, and every binder control’s own text. Tabular numerals. The page default.

figure.purpose: The value beside each graduated rule and the step number. The page’s one heavy element, and it stays in ink.

deviation.purpose: The words under a rule stating its standing against its band; a measured cell’s unit; a step’s purpose and aside in italic.

note.purpose: Written notes, typed or saved: 16px at 1.5 leading, at the 65ch measure. Also the size a recorded figure reads at, and the field size wherever the pointer is coarse.

small-print.purpose: Target chips, basis notes, rule anchors, fat breakdown, plan sub-lines, cross-flags, version-strip meta, import errors.

rules.purpose: Paper catalogue: Stroke weights for the graduated rule, the table, the strike, and the drawn controls. Depth is rule weight; nothing else conveys it. Hover and focus carry their own 2px weight because 1.5px renders as 1px at DPR 1.

focus.exception: .is-landing-focus:focus — a plain :focus rule for the fork’s landing focus after a mouse-driven Save, which Chrome’s modality tracking would otherwise leave ringless. The one documented exception.
focus.purpose: Implemented paper focus treatment; app treatment remains to be specified. The one focus treatment, provably heavier than the 1px outline pointed-at content carries and a different sign from a picked control’s fill. Never colour, never position.

state.picked: A picked or pressed CONTROL fills pen blue edge to edge, border and all, with paper-coloured text. No bold, no underline, no outline of its own. An independent on/off is a square and a word — only the 13px square fills.
state.pointedAt: Content the page is pointing at — a marked table row, the open batch, the current version, a pressed Show changes — reads bold plus a 1px ink outline offset 2px, in place.
state.recorded: Anything the maker typed or saved reads pen blue and keeps it after saving. An absence (“not measured”) is ink.
state.notInForce: One ink strike at 1.2px — a skipped step, a superseded value, a removed row or step. Beside the replacement where there is room, beneath it for a paragraph.
state.forcedColors: The picked fill survives as a fill, repainted in the system Highlight with HighlightText, so state and focus never collapse into the same outline. A focused picked control switches its ring to CanvasText.

breakpoints.name: spread-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The two-column spread becomes one column in the order band, ingredients, side, method, foot — side BEFORE method, so the formulation note stays near its table. Page gap narrows to 20px; the pen foot collapses with it.

breakpoints.name: touch-union
breakpoints.purpose: Touch sizes. Buttons, selects, ink fields, segmented options, defect toggles and text controls take a 44px minimum height; an axis stop grows in HEIGHT only, to 38x44; .ink-field and .prose-field read 16px. A union, not a replacement: a narrowed desktop window still exercises touch mode, and a real touch device is caught however wide it is.

breakpoints.name: narrow-layout
breakpoints.purpose: Width only. The version row collapses to one column and the axis track takes its 216px geometry with 44x44 stops. Track geometry is deliberately NOT in the touch union: at 1366 the axes sit in three 213.3px columns, where a 216px track overflows into its neighbour.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Page padding shrinks to 20px, the margin’s prose field drops to the control size, both save ceremonies may wrap, and the ingredient table scrolls inside its own region rather than overflowing the page.

breakpoints.name: wide-touch
breakpoints.purpose: A tablet held in the hand at a desktop width (sketch 009). Axis and segmented caption lines reserve two lines of caption height so they sit level with the field captions beside them, and Clear takes its 44px target as an overflowing ::after hit area so the line box never grows.

breakpoints.name: forced-colors
breakpoints.purpose: Repaints the picked fill in the system Highlight rather than removing it.

table.purpose: The ingredient table’s layout is fixed and its leading constant so a marked row’s bold weight moves nothing. Cells are border-box, so a declared column width is the whole column. The name column is the single unsized column, absorbing what the sized columns leave; rows read in step order under step-group heads.

battery.captionLine: Reserves Clear’s height marked or not (24px desktop, 44px narrow touch, two caption lines at wide touch) so picking moves nothing.
battery.clearance: 12px between a desktop axis stop and the core/declared hairline, carried as the declared column’s own padding-left rather than a column gap.
battery.purpose: The record pen’s own instrument: six axes in one grid with the defects, a 1px hairline at the two-thirds line, two cue rows heading the columns. A genuinely different DOM shape below 760px, not a media-scoped layout.

scope.implementedCatalogue: Paper Recipe Sheets and batch/tasting logs; legacy app reuse is transitional.
scope.approvedAppDirection: Option B destination palette with revised Ingredients green and preview neutrals approved 2026-09-21 in DESIGN.md frontmatter. Not yet implemented. No recipe-specific colors. Interaction, feedback, and derived state treatments unresolved.
scope.tonalRamps: Preview metadata only; not approved UI colors.
scope.emptyShadowsAndMotion: No implemented entries in this catalogue; empty arrays are not global prohibitions.

narrative.overview:
The cookbook remains the material reference for Recipe Sheets and batch/tasting logs. Around those paper surfaces, Sprinkles has a colorful app interface for navigation, recipe context, history, and supporting tools. The two contexts belong to one product: paper supports reading, making, and recording; the app interface supports finding, choosing, and continuing work. The retired name “Sprinkles Jar” is not an interface label.

**The Context Boundary Rule.** Apply paper rules to Recipe Sheets, batch/tasting logs, and print, not to every element on a recipe route. Recipe-level name and description, History, provenance, version selection, and navigation belong to app context. Sheet title, Sheet description, ingredients, Method, and Notes belong to the version's Recipe Sheet. Batch records keep the paper and pen treatment. A shared route does not imply a shared visual context.

| Context | Approved direction | Implementation status |
|---|---|---|
| App interface | Bright, colorful, approachable; the approved Option B destination palette and neutral set. Color identifies and guides, never judges a result. | Base palette and neutrals approved; interaction and feedback colors, derived states, type roles, shapes, depth, motion, and components remain unresolved. Existing paper-styled shell/history controls are transitional. |
| Recipe Sheet and batch/tasting log | Paper, ink, pen blue, restrained rules, readable prose and precise quantities. | Existing tokens and component catalogue below. Proposed highlighter role remains unresolved. |
| Print | Black on white, with room for handwritten records and a stable reference to the version. | Print behavior is owned by the print surface brief; screen paper color is not a requirement to print a background. |

Home composition belongs in its surface brief. Mockups are exploration evidence, not token specifications: photographs, handwriting, slogans, and exact component geometry are not approved merely because they appear in a preferred concept.
keyCharacteristics: Two explicit visual contexts: colorful app interface and paper Recipe Sheets/records.
Four implemented paper color roles, plus approved app destination colors and neutrals; no recipe-specific colors.
Paper prose uses the text face; measured quantities use the grotesk with tabular numerals.
Paper controls preserve the binder's ink outlines, pen-blue selection, and distinct focus indication.
Across both contexts, color never carries a verdict; meaning and interaction state remain legible without color.
Approved direction is distinct from shipped components and unresolved visual choices.

rules.name: The Context Boundary Rule
rules.body: Apply paper rules to Recipe Sheets, batch/tasting logs, and print, not to every element on a recipe route. Recipe-level name and description, History, provenance, version selection, and navigation belong to app context. Sheet title, Sheet description, ingredients, Method, and Notes belong to the version's Recipe Sheet. Batch records keep the paper and pen treatment. A shared route does not imply a shared visual context.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Within the paper contexts, printed matter is ink black; recorded matter is pen blue; the two never mix on one element. A value that is half plan and half record is two values. The record keeps its blue after saving — it is the maker's, and saving changes form, not ink.

rules.name: The No-Verdict Rule
rules.body: No colour anywhere carries pass, fail, warning, or uncertainty. A figure's standing against its band is stated in words beside the figure; estimated or unreviewed data says so as a word in the Data column; a malformed measurement is a sentence under the field and `aria-invalid`, never a red line. A picked control's pen-blue fill is not a verdict — it is the record's own ink saying *the maker chose this*.

rules.name: The Bookcloth Rule
rules.body: In paper contexts, bookcloth names regions or draws the existing band-sub-row hairline. This role does not constrain green or other identity colors in the app interface.

rules.name: The Counted-in-Grotesk Rule
rules.body: Any value that can be weighed, measured, or compared sits in the grotesk with tabular numerals. Prose sits in the text face. The step number is a figure, so it is grotesk.

rules.name: The Lowercase-Unit Rule
rules.body: Units keep their case everywhere, including inside uppercase running heads.

rules.name: The Placeholder Rule
rules.body: A placeholder is an example in ink small print, italic — never a default, never pen blue. A blank field still saves as blank.

rules.name: The Caption-and-Helper Rule
rules.body: A caption is uppercase and labels exactly one input. A sentence that explains rather than labels is a *helper*, sentence-cased, and it sits beside the caption as a sibling — never folded into it, where `text-transform` would shout it.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Wherever the pointer is coarse, `.ink-field` and `.prose-field` read at the note size (16px). Below 16px iOS Safari zooms the page on field focus, which moves the record under the maker's thumb; the app's earlier 13px touch size is retired.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Every caption that sits atop its own content — field captions, axis names, segmented captions, group cues — carries one 6px gap (`--gap-xs`) to it, whatever it captions. One rule for every caption site.

rules.name: The Drawn-For Rule
rules.body: A rule governs only the case it was drawn for. The touch union also matches every narrow width, where a 44px caption line was drawn and verified; applying the wide-touch reserve across the union silently overwrote that drawing at 680, 580, 480 and 393. When a new case appears, it gets its own condition — never a widened old one.

rules.name: The Capability Rule
rules.body: Touch *sizes* read the pointer. Touch *layouts* read the width. A height can grow anywhere safely; a track width cannot, because no layout has been drawn for touch-sized stops at desktop widths.

rules.name: The Paper-Is-Flat Rule
rules.body: Within a Recipe Sheet or batch/tasting log, nothing floats above the paper. If an element needs to stand apart, it gets a heavier rule, an ink outline, or the pen's fill — never a shadow.

rules.name: The Focus-Heavier-than-State Rule
rules.body: One focus rule at the browser's own `:focus-visible` boundary draws a 2px ink outline offset 2px — heavier than the 1px outline any pointed-at content carries, and a different sign from a pressed control's fill. A focused element that is also stateful reads both. There is exactly one documented exception: `.is-landing-focus:focus`, a plain `:focus` rule that makes the fork's landing focus visible after a mouse-driven Save, which Chrome's modality tracking would otherwise leave ringless.

rules.name: The Hover-Is-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hover thickens a border from 1px to a whole 2px and removes exactly that much padding, so the box never changes size — 1.5px renders as 1px at DPR 1, which is why hover needs its own token rather than borrowing the baseline. A joined control thickens in place and stacks above its neighbours. Weight, never position or hue.

dos: Do establish whether an element belongs to app context, a Recipe Sheet, a batch/tasting log, or print before applying visual rules.
Do preserve the implemented paper tokens and distinguish approved app tokens from shipped implementation.
Do keep destination accents distinct from ink that communicates plan and actual records; do not assign recipe-specific colors.
Do keep keyboard focus discernible from selected state, preserve semantic controls, and make touch targets usable.
Do state balance, uncertainty, errors, and provenance in words; color never supplies a verdict.
Do keep units correctly cased, quantities legible, and required/error feedback attached to its control.
Do use the paper catalogue for paper typography, outlines, pen selection, step order, and print behavior.
Do distinguish approved direction, observed implementation, and unresolved design choices.
Do keep page composition in surface briefs and reusable visual rules in this document.
donts: Don't impose the paper palette's four colors on Home, navigation, recipe context, History, Ingredients, Kitchen, or consultations.
Don't extend paper's flatness, square corners, no-motion treatment, or image restrictions into app-wide bans.
Don't add shadows, gradients, rounded cards, or animation inside paper contexts merely because the surrounding app can use a different treatment.
Don't introduce app palette values, fonts, shadows, radii, or motion timings from exploratory mocks without a design decision.
Don't treat sidecar tonal-ramp previews as approved additional colors.
Don't use color to encode success, failure, warning, or uncertainty, or make interaction state depend on color alone.
Don't paint recipe-level metadata as recorded pen content merely because it shares a route with the Sheet.
Don't call the surrounding interface “Sprinkles Jar.” Use the approved section names and vocabulary.
